commits.subject: feat(app): FIX-1305 — alias 308 to www + origin-auth header check (report mode) in middleware (cc-230)

stopped_items: No STOP fired. All 9 /api/cron/* routes carry the bearer gate. The middleware's first statement was the BOT_PATTERNS 404, and the build is green on the edge runtime. No permission prompt fired.

Scope change mid-run (Craig's delta, two messages): I folded D0 (the alias 308), robots.txt Crawl-delay, the four crawlers, the Verified bots skip WAF rule, and probe 4 into the same commit, under the delta's subject. Because of the delta I filed FIX-1306 (alternates.canonical), so fixes_filed is not the prompt's [].

Deviation from the delta's literal code: new URL(pathname + search, origin) treats a //host path as protocol-relative and would make the alias an open redirect. The target is now built by assigning pathname/search onto a fixed https://www.civitics.com URL, with a unit test.

Deviation, middleware shape: the existing body moved unchanged into routeRequest(), so D6's miss stamp lands on every return (early 404/308/429 included) without editing eleven return sites. The source-text test pins the order two ways: file order (decideAliasRedirect, then decideOriginAuth, then BOT_PATTERNS.some, then checkRateLimit) and order inside middleware() (alias, then origin, then routeRequest).

Scope note: besides the named FIX-570 paragraph, I also corrected a second stale 'fail-open' comment, at the limiter call (old :242-243). It is in middleware.ts. FIX-1304's two comments, in ratelimit.ts and upstash-usage.ts, are untouched.

Not verifiable from here: whether the Cloudflare Transform Rule is stamping (read 1 (c)). Under Attack hides the header on probe 3, and in report mode a non-stamping rule still serves 200, so platform-snapshot.yml staying green does not prove it. The proof is cc-231's count of cf-ray=yes misses.
